# dsh-session-isolation
中文说明

Give every session in a chosen DeepSeek Harness workspace its own working
directory — new sessions s

tart there, and existing sessions get one the first
time they are opened — without turning each sess
ion into a separate workspace.
`@local/dsh-session-isolation` is a local DSH bundle with two halves:

- **Host** — listens to `agent/created`; when a session starts (`startup`), gets a
fresh conversatio

n (`clear`), or is an existing session resumed while still at
the workspace root, it
creates `<works

pace>\<baseDir>\<session-id>` and switches the session's
`working-directory` projection to that dire

ctory.
- **Browser** — adds a folder button to the conversation header (next to DSH's
built-in "Open

in…" split button) that opens the session directory in the OS
file manager, and repairs file addres

ses that DSH builds against the stale
workspace root (v1.2.0).

Session ownership never changes: `SessionHeader.cwd` stays the workspace root, so
the sidebar keeps
grouping the session under its original workspace.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Features

- **Per-session working directory** — agents start in `_sessions\<session-id>`
and only write there

unless they explicitly go elsewhere.
- **No workspace surgery** — no new workspace entries, no `Sess

ionHeader` rewrite,
no changes to DSH's profile or workspace registry.
- **Existing sessions too** —

a session that is still at its workspace root gets
its own directory on first entry (a new session,

a cleared session, or a
session resumed after installing the bundle). Sessions that already have th

eir
own working directory — including an `_sessions` folder — are never moved.
- **Subagents include

d by default** — every subagent session gets its own folder
(can be turned off).
- **Never blocks a

session** — any isolation failure is logged as a warning and
the session silently keeps the workspac

e root.
- **Header button only where it makes sense** — it queries a read-only Host route
instead of

guessing a path, and stays hidden for sessions that are not isolated.
- **Client-side address repai

r (v1.2.0)** — file links and file cards in chat open
correctly in the document preview even though

the working directory is no
longer the workspace root.
## Screenshots

button:

## Requirements

- DSH Desktop **0.2.1-rc.2 or later** (tested on 0.2.1-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.3 and
0.2.1-rc.5).
- The profi

le enables `@deepseek-ai/dsh-working-directory` and the browser module
system — both are on by defau

lt in the desktop build.
- Windows was the primary target; the Host half uses only `node:` built-ins

and
`path` semantics, so other platforms work as long as the configured workspace
paths are absolut

nd
`path` semantics, so other platforms work as long as the configured workspace
paths are absolute.
## Install

The package is **not published to npm**. DSH links a local bundle into the current
profile and mount
s the Host row declared by the bundle's own `cordis.patch.yml`.

1. Clone this repository into a stable directory, for example
`D:\dsh-session-isolation`.
2. Edit `c

ordis.patch.yml`: replace the example
`workspaces` entry with your own workspace root (absolute path

; write doubled
backslashes in YAML on Windows).
3. Install the folder as a bundle and restart DSH D

esktop:
- DSH Desktop → **Plugins** → install a bundle from a folder → select this
directory; or
- f

rom a DSH session that exposes the plugin manager:
`plugin_manager install_bundle target=<repo path>

om a DSH session that exposes the plugin manager:
`plugin_manager install_bundle target=<repo path>`

A local install is a **link**: DSH uses the folder in place, so keep it where it
is (moving or delet
ing it disables the plugin).
## Configuration
The inserted `session-isolation` row in `cordis.patch.yml`:
| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| `workspaces` | `string[]` | required | Absolute workspace roots. Only sessions whose `header.cwd`

equals one of them are isolated. |
| `baseDir` | `string` | `_sessions` | Directory name under each

workspace. Relative paths are resolved per workspace; absolute paths are used as-is. |
| `isolateSub
agents` | `boolean` | `true` | Also give subagent sessions their own directory. |

Invalid configuration makes the plugin fail at activation (the row shows as
failed) instead of silen

ion makes the plugin fail at activation (the row shows as
failed) instead of silently doing nothing.
## How it works
## Compatibility

Tested with DSH **0.2.1-rc.2**, **0.2.1-rc.3** and **0.2.1-rc.5** on Windows
11. The bundle only use
s public, stable contracts and patches no DSH internals:

- Host: `agent/created` (serial, awaited listener), the `workingDirectory`
service, `webServer.regis

ter` + `connection.requestRejection`, `sessions.get`.
- Browser: `dsh.client` packaging (`exports[".

/client"]` →
`/plugins/<name>/client.js`), the `conversation.session.header.utilities` slot,
the `sl
ots` / `locale` / `sessions` services, and DSH's `/open-in-app` routes.

Behaviour of the host and client contracts above was re-checked against
0.2.1-rc.3 and again against

0.2.1-rc.5 (2026-10-30) — working directory
service, `agent/created` signature, `webServer.register

` +
`connection.requestRejection`, slot registration (the bundle's header button is
registered and a

ctive), file-address grammar and `/open-in-app` body validation
are unchanged — no code changes were

required. v1.2.2 (2026-10-30) additionally
isolates **resumed** sessions that are still at the work

space root, so existing
sessions get a folder the first time they are opened after installing the bu

ry lookup for a few seconds after a miss (and never cache a
miss), so a session restored while the w

indow boots still gets its button.
Runtime dependencies: none (Node built-ins only).
